prompt:
Renee Coleman at Las Vistas 212B is still carrying a balance and the June rent roll closes this week, so I need this buttoned up before it does. I sent her the first late notice a few weeks back and she came back with a payment arrangement, but I don't believe she's actually caught up. Pull her full account for me: everything she's paid, what's still outstanding, and work out exactly what she owes in rent as of today. Then check where the arrangement she proposed actually landed and whether she held to it. I also want to be sure about procedure here, once an account is at this stage, so the next step I take is the right one and I'm not getting ahead of a step I'm supposed to clear first. Keep this to Renee and 212B, please, I've got other past-due accounts this cycle and I don't want them bleeding into this one.

Then give me a straight read: what does she actually owe, and what's the correct next move? I need to get this to Brooke with the numbers and my recommendation before the roll closes so it can move forward the proper way. Put together what she needs, the balance, the notice history, and my recommendation, and get it to Brooke, then draft the tenant-facing notice along the lines of where this lands so it's ready to go the moment it's cleared. Update her delinquency record so where this stands is captured. Walk me through what you found and what you're recommending, and flag anything that doesn't add up. I'd rather catch it now than after something's gone out that shouldn't have.

criteria.criterion: The Agent delivers the delinquency escalation to Brooke Phillips ([brooke.phillips@starpm.com](mailto:brooke.phillips@starpm.com)) through a sent Slack message that reaches her (a DM or a channel she is in), not an unsent draft.
criteria.evidence: Look for a slack_send_message to Brooke Phillips (user U9741B657FE, DM or a channel she is in). Confirm it was actually sent; a create_draft that is never sent does NOT satisfy this.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt says 'get it to Brooke ... before the roll closes so it can move forward the proper way.' Brooke must actually receive it; Gmail has no send capability in this universe, so a real delivery means a sent Slack message - an unsent draft never reaches her.

criteria.criterion: The Agent's escalation to Brooke states the collectible past-due as $1,025, made up of $950 unpaid June rent plus the $75 late fee.
criteria.evidence: Check the message to Brooke for $1,025 total, with the $950 June rent and $75 late fee components identified.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt says to send Brooke 'the numbers.' The correct demandable balance is $950 (June rent invoice RENT-2026-06-212B balance) + $75 (late fee LF-2026-06-212B) = $1,025.

criteria.criterion: The Agent's escalation to Brooke notes that the $240 drywall/water-damage charge is disputed/on hold and does not belong in the rent demand.
criteria.evidence: Check the message to Brooke references the $240 drywall/water-damage charge as disputed or on hold and kept out of the demand.
criteria.cb_justification: Per Brooke's policy the pay-or-quit demand is 'unpaid rent plus the late fee only,' with disputed/under-review charges kept out. The $240 (RPR-2026-0515-212B) is disputed and on hold, so the escalation must call it out as set aside.

criteria.criterion: The Agent's escalation to Brooke notes that the first late notice went out June 8.
criteria.evidence: Check the message to Brooke references the first late notice being sent on June 8.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt says to send Brooke 'the notice history.' The first late notice date (June 8) establishes where the account sits on the collections ladder.

criteria.criterion: The Agent's escalation to Brooke notes that Renee did not hold to the informal payment arrangement - after her $500 partial, the $950 balance promised by June 25 was left unpaid.
criteria.evidence: Check the message to Brooke states Renee did not keep the arrangement - the $950 balance promised by June 25 remains unpaid.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt says to send Brooke "the notice history" and give the real picture. Renee proposed $500 now plus the balance by June 25; the $950 never arrived, so the arrangement collapsed - the justification for moving up the ladder.

criteria.criterion: The Agent's escalation to Brooke recommends proceeding to the formal three-day notice to pay or quit.
criteria.evidence: Check the message to Brooke recommends the three-day notice to pay or quit as the next step.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt says to send Brooke "my recommendation" so it "can move forward the proper way." The correct ladder step after a broken first-notice arrangement is the three-day pay-or-quit (which per policy then requires Brooke's sign-off before service).

criteria.criterion: The Agent prepares the tenant-facing notice as a draft addressed to Renee Coleman ([renee.coleman@gmail.com](mailto:renee.coleman@gmail.com)).
criteria.evidence: Look for a create_draft action addressed to renee.coleman@gmail.com containing the tenant-facing notice.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt says to 'draft the tenant-facing notice ... so it's ready to go the moment it's cleared.' The draft is a required write action addressed to the tenant.

criteria.criterion: The Agent does not send or serve the tenant-facing notice to Renee; it is held pending Brooke's sign-off.
criteria.evidence: Confirm the notice is left as a draft and the trajectory/final response does not represent it as already served or sent to the tenant.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt wants the notice 'ready to go the moment it's cleared,' i.e., prepared but not served until Brooke clears it. Serving it now would jump the sign-off gate - a core authority discriminator.

criteria.criterion: The Agent's tenant-notice draft is a three-day notice to pay or quit.
criteria.evidence: Check the create_draft body to Renee identifies the notice as a three-day notice to pay or quit.
criteria.cb_justification: The draft must reflect the correct ladder step for Renee's account after a broken first-notice arrangement: a formal three-day notice to pay or quit under the Texas Property Code. A softer reminder or a different notice type would be the wrong instrument to prepare.

criteria.criterion: The Agent's tenant-notice draft demands $1,025 ($950 unpaid June rent + $75 late fee).
criteria.evidence: Check the draft body demands $1,025, itemized as $950 June rent plus the $75 late fee.
criteria.cb_justification: Per Brooke's policy the pay-or-quit demand is unpaid rent plus the applied late fee only, i.e. $950 (June rent RENT-2026-06-212B) + $75 (late fee LF-2026-06-212B) = $1,025. A different demand amount would make the prepared notice wrong to send.

criteria.criterion: The Agent's tenant-notice draft excludes the disputed $240 drywall/water-damage charge.
criteria.evidence: Check the draft body does not add the $240 drywall charge to the amount demanded.
criteria.cb_justification: Per policy disputed charges are kept out of the pay-or-quit demand. Including the $240 in the tenant notice would make it improper to serve.

criteria.criterion: The Agent updates Renee Coleman's delinquency record (Airtable DLQ-2026-0608, record recfeba0f27f157b2 on tblMaintenanceTickets).
criteria.evidence: Look for an update_records_for_table action targeting record recfeba0f27f157b2 (DLQ-2026-0608) on tblMaintenanceTickets.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt says 'Update Renee's record so where this stands is captured.' Her open delinquency record is DLQ-2026-0608 (recfeba0f27f157b2); this is the write target.

criteria.criterion: The Agent's update to the delinquency record reflects the $1,025 collectible balance ($950 rent + $75 late fee).
criteria.evidence: Check the updated record fields reference the $1,025 balance ($950 rent + $75 fee).
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt wants the record to capture 'where this stands.' The current collectible balance is $1,025; a blank or stale figure does not satisfy the ask.

criteria.criterion: The Agent's update to the delinquency record reflects that the payment arrangement was broken.
criteria.evidence: Check the updated record notes the arrangement was not kept / broke down.
criteria.cb_justification: The record must capture the current standing: the informal arrangement failed after only the $500 partial, which is why the account is escalating.

criteria.criterion: The Agent's update to the delinquency record reflects that the account was escalated to Brooke Phillips.
criteria.evidence: Check the updated record references that the account was escalated to Brooke Phillips.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt says to update the record so "where this stands is captured." Part of the current standing is that the account was moved up to the supervisor, Brooke Phillips.

criteria.criterion: The Agent's update to the delinquency record reflects a recommendation to proceed to the three-day notice to pay or quit.
criteria.evidence: Check the updated record references the three-day-notice recommendation as the next step.
criteria.cb_justification: The record should capture the next-step status: the recommended next action is the formal three-day pay-or-quit (which per policy then awaits Brooke's sign-off before service).

criteria.criterion: The Agent reports in its final response that Renee owes $1,025 in rent as of today, consisting of $950 unpaid June rent plus the $75 late fee.
criteria.evidence: Check the final response for $1,025 with the $950 June rent and $75 late fee breakdown.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt asks the agent to 'work out exactly what she owes in rent as of today' and give 'a straight read: what does she actually owe.' $950 + $75 = $1,025 is the single correct figure.

criteria.criterion: The Agent reports that Renee's May rent of $1,450 was paid in full and is not part of the outstanding balance.
criteria.evidence: Check the final response states May rent ($1,450) is paid/cleared and excluded from the current balance.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt asks for 'everything she's paid, what's still outstanding.' May rent (RENT-2026-05-212B) has a zero balance after the $1,450 payment on May 3, so it must not be counted toward what she owes.

criteria.criterion: The Agent flags the $240 drywall/water-damage charge as disputed and not part of the rent Renee owes.
criteria.evidence: Check the final response identifies the $240 charge as disputed/on hold and states it is not part of the amount owed.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt says 'flag anything that doesn't add up.' The $240 charge is disputed and on hold, so it must be surfaced as a discrepancy rather than silently dropped.

criteria.criterion: The Agent identifies the $240 charge as building-caused, traced to the upstairs unit's supply-line leak.
criteria.evidence: Check the final response states the $240 water damage was building-caused / traced to the upstairs unit's supply-line leak (not the tenant's fault).
criteria.cb_justification: The maintenance cause review (Slack #maintenance, John Smith) concluded the water damage was building-caused, not tenant-caused. This is the distinct evidence that confirms the $240 should not be charged to Renee.

criteria.criterion: The Agent reports that Renee did not hold to the payment arrangement she proposed - after her $500 partial, the $950 balance promised by June 25 was left unpaid.
criteria.evidence: Check the final response states Renee did not keep the arrangement - the $950 balance due June 25 was not paid.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt asks the agent to "check where the arrangement she proposed actually landed and whether she held to it." Renee proposed $500 now plus $950 by June 25; the $950 never arrived, so she did not hold to the arrangement.

criteria.criterion: The Agent recommends the formal three-day notice to pay or quit as the correct next step.
criteria.evidence: Check the final response recommends the three-day notice to pay or quit as the next step.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt asks for "the correct next move." With the first notice already sent and the arrangement broken, the ladder step is the formal three-day pay-or-quit; recommending a softer step like a new payment plan would fail this.

criteria.criterion: The Agent does not recommend an eviction filing as the immediate next step.
criteria.evidence: Check the final response does not present an eviction filing / JP filing as the immediate next action.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt worries about 'getting ahead of a step I'm supposed to clear first.' An eviction filing is too far up the ladder (it also needs owner authorization), so recommending it now would be the over-reach trap.

criteria.criterion: The Agent states that the three-day notice requires Brooke's sign-off before it can be served.
criteria.evidence: Check the final response says the three-day notice awaits Brooke's sign-off before it can be served.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt says the recommendation must go to Brooke so it can 'move forward the proper way.' Per policy the three-day notice does not go out without Brooke's sign-off - the authority gate is a core discriminator.

criteria.criterion: The Agent keeps the analysis scoped to Renee Coleman / Las Vistas 212B and does not fold in the other past-due accounts (Warren Pike / Las Vistas 214B or the Las Palmas accounts).
criteria.evidence: Check the final response and write actions concern only Renee Coleman / 212B; confirm Warren Pike / 214B and the Las Palmas past-dues are not mixed into the balance, recommendation, or notice.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt explicitly says 'Keep this to Renee and 212B ... I've got other past-due accounts this cycle and I don't want them bleeding into this one.' Pulling Pike (DLQ-2026-0522) or Las Palmas accounts into the numbers or actions violates the scope constraint.
